summary: Threaded the bounded ADR-026 log subject through every ADR-026 clause 3 site. The identity-bearing sites now build the subject with LogSubject.Create(itemId, identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath): ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.LogOutcome (request.JellyfinItemId plus request.MediaIdentity), both MetadataReconciliationProcessor provider-error metadata-read-failure paths (the identity created by MediaIdentityFactory.TryCreate), and RadarrMetadataReader.LogMatch / SonarrMetadataReader.LogMatch. The mixed MetadataReconciliationProcessor.Discard site gained a Discard(Guid itemId, string? primaryPath, string reason) overload: the two-argument overload used by the pre-identity discards passes no path, and the six changed-basis discards after identity creation pass identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath. LibraryWorkWorker (processed and retry-scheduled) and ArrTagsLifecycleService (item removed) use the item-id-only LogSubject.Create overload. The four sites ADR-026 clause 3 marks unchanged were not modified. tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogRedactionTests.cs adds 10 per-site theories over the six verbosity levels (60 cases) covering the file-name-only subject, the mixed-site path/fallback behavior, the item-id fallbacks, and sentinel-freedom at every level.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The artwork coordinator emits the file name when the identity/path is available.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: LogOutcome builds LogSubject.Create(request.JellyfinItemId, request.MediaIdentity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath) and interpolates the subject (src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.cs); LogRedactionTests.ArtworkSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts the message contains 'item example.mkv', no '/', and no item identifier at the levels where the Information line is enabled.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The metadata reconciliation processor's metadata-read-failure line emits the file name when the identity/path is available.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Both MetadataReadFailed paths (the reader-threw catch and the failed-read result) build the subject from the identity created by MediaIdentityFactory.TryCreate (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs); LogRedactionTests.MetadataReadFailureSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts 'item example.mkv', no '/', no item identifier, and pins the failed-read reason line; MetadataReadFailureSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenNoPathIsAvailable proves the same identity-bearing line falls back when the identity has no primary path.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Sonarr/Radarr metadata readers emit the file name when the identity/path is available.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: RadarrMetadataReader.LogMatch and SonarrMetadataReader.LogMatch build LogSubject.Create(identity.JellyfinItemId, identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath); LogRedactionTests.RadarrMatchSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts 'item example.mkv' and SonarrMatchSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts 'item s02e05.mkv', each with no '/', no item identifier, and no sentinel.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The mixed MetadataReconciliationProcessor.Discard site uses the file name when available and falls back to the item id otherwise; it does not thread a path where none exists.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Discard(Guid, string?, string) builds LogSubject.Create(itemId, primaryPath); the six changed-basis discards after identity creation pass identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath, and the two-argument overload used by the version-mismatch, item-missing, identity-creation-failure, ineligibility, and connection-unavailable discards delegates with null (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs). LogRedactionTests covers the path case (MetadataDiscardSubjectIsTheFileNameWhenAPathIsAvailableAtEveryVerbosity), the identity-without-path case (MetadataDiscardSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenTheIdentityHasNoPath), and the no-identity case (MetadataDiscardSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenNoIdentityExists); each pins the exact discard branch reason.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The work worker and lifecycle removal event use the documented item-id fallback.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: LibraryWorkWorker.LogProcessed/LogRetryScheduled build LogSubject.Create(item.Key.ItemId); ArrTagsLifecycleService builds LogSubject.Create(e.ItemId) for the item-removed record. LogRedactionTests.WorkWorkerSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity and LifecycleRemovalSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity assert the D-format item identifier, no '/', no file name, and no sentinel at every verbosity.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Per-site tests prove no directory appears and that the mixed site falls back correctly.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AssertFileNameSubject asserts the message names 'item <file name>', contains no '/', and no longer contains the replaced item identifier; AssertItemIdSubject asserts 'item <D-format id>', no '/', and neither file name. The 10 theories run over all six verbosity levels; AssertNoSentinel(run) is asserted on every case, including the levels where the line is gated off (record count 0).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Phase 15 threading portion: the file-name-only subject is emitted where a path is available and the item id where it is not, including the mixed discard site.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The code changes and the 60 new LogRedactionTests cases above; the remaining phase-15 criteria (bounded render classification, ADR-020 clause 4 amendment, canonical documentation, security review, F8 resolution) are owned by tasks 15.3 and 15.4 and are untouched.

interpretations.question: Which available identity's path the mixed discard threads when both the basis identity and the publish-time re-resolved identity exist.
interpretations.chosen: The basis identity created at the metadata-read stage (identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath) at all six post-identity discards.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 3 describes the mixed site as called 'where an identity exists (changed-basis discards after identity creation)'; the basis identity is the identity the queued work was based on and the only one present at every such branch (the publish-time TryCreate can fail).
interpretations.impact: At a changed-basis discard the log names the file observed when the work's identity was captured; if the item's primary path changes within that processing window, the earlier file name is emitted. Log output only; no persisted state or user-visible behavior.

interpretations.question: Which code paths constitute 'the metadata-read-failure line' in the processor.
interpretations.chosen: Both provider-error paths that emit ArrTagsLogEvent.MetadataReadFailed: the reader-threw catch and the failed-read result.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 3 names the identity-bearing metadata-read-failure line by its event/shape; both paths emit the identical message shape after identity creation and before the same fallback semantics apply.
interpretations.impact: Consistent subjects on both failure paths; no behavior change beyond the subject.

interpretations.question: What the worker fallback replaces: only the item-id component or the whole WorkItemKey text.
interpretations.chosen: The whole WorkItemKey text is replaced by the item-id-only subject, LogSubject.Create(item.Key.ItemId).
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 1 replaces the emitted Jellyfin item identifier with the bounded subject, and clause 3 lists LibraryWorkWorker as a fallback site '(item id only)' reached via WorkItemKey.
interpretations.impact: The Debug records change from 'WorkItemKey(<N-format id>, <connection>, <surface>)' to the D-format item identifier. No persisted state or non-log behavior changes.

test_sensitivity: Reverting the artwork subject to the raw item id failed ArtworkSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity in 3 cases (Information, Debug, Trace); probe reverted.

Reverting both metadata-read-failure subjects to LogSubject.Create(item.Key.ItemId) failed MetadataReadFailureSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity in 4 cases (Warning, Information, Debug, Trace); probe reverted.
Reverting the Radarr and Sonarr LogMatch subjects to the item id failed their file-name theories in 2 cases each (Debug, Trace); probe reverted.
Ignoring primaryPath in the three-argument Discard helper failed MetadataDiscardSubjectIsTheFileNameWhenAPathIsAvailableAtEveryVerbosity in 3 cases (Information, Debug, Trace); probe reverted.

Replacing the fallback with a non-item-id subject failed MetadataReadFailureSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenNoPathIsAvailable (4 cases), MetadataDiscardSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenTheIdentityHasNoPath (3 cases), and MetadataDiscardSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenNoIdentityExists (3 cases); probe reverted.
Reverting the worker subject to item.Key.ToString() failed WorkWorkerSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity in 2 cases (Debug, Trace); probe reverted.

Emitting an N-format identifier at the lifecycle-removal site failed LifecycleRemovalSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity in 2 cases (Debug, Trace); probe reverted. The lifecycle site's item-id fallback is byte-identical to its pre-task D-format output, so reverting that site to its pre-task code cannot fail the test by construction; the probe used a different subject format to show the assertion is sensitive.
All probes were applied as direct source edits and reverted by restoring byte-identical copies (diff clean); the final LogRedactionTests run passed 125/125 and the final full suite passed 1577/1640.

known_limitations: The explicit fallback boundaries (LibraryWorkWorker, ArrTagsLifecycleService) and the pre-identity metadata discards emit the item identifier and never a file name; this is the ADR-026 clause 3 documented behavior for boundaries with no media identity or path. The lifecycle-removal output is byte-identical to its pre-task D-format item id; the worker record changed from the WorkItemKey text to the item-id-only subject.

At a changed-basis discard the emitted name is the file name from the identity captured at the metadata-read stage, not a re-read path: if the item's primary path changes within the same processing window after identity creation, the discard line carries the earlier file name. Log output only; no persisted state or user-visible behavior.

F8 remains open. Task 15.3 owns emitting the bounded render classification on the artwork log line, and task 15.4 owns the ADR-020 clause 4 amendment, the README/architecture/limitations reconciliation, the logging security review, and the F8 resolution; until 15.4 those current-state documents continue to describe the shipped v1.1 logging behavior.
